text:
mike_sales: Quick sync — FinLedger wants an enterprise commit. They expect mixed chat+embed traffic, target p95 tail latency <300ms for chat. Rough numbers from their PO: peak ~600 qps, average 40 tokens per chat request, p95 token length ~220, embeddings steady at ~120 req/s. They asked if 16 reserved GPUs + burst is sane and whether we should do KV preheat. Also CC: security questionnaire asks about KMS/audit — need a short list to hand them.

ben_ops: Thanks — couple clarifying q's first: is that 600 qps chat-only or includes api multiplexing with embeddings? Also do they want single-region AZ affinity?

mike_sales: It's mixed: chat is ~80% of traffic by token volume, embeddings 20% by request count. They want multi-AZ but prefer traffic in us-east1 primarily.

anya_ml: For a quantized 70B-ish working set with avg seq 40 and p95 220, throughput per A100-ish GPU will vary a lot by quantization/kv cache hit rate. If we assume 4–6 RPS per GPU for p95 chat (conservative), 600 qps peak implies ~100–150 GPUs if you try to hit p95 on-host at full peak without batching/kv. BUT with good KV prefix caching and batching for short sequences, reserved pool can be much smaller. My rough recommendation: start with 12 reserved GPUs + autoscale burst to 24 (max_burst 12) + aggressive KV warmup. Synthetic warmers preheat hot prefixes for their top ~5k prompts.

ben_ops: Adding concrete config snippet for ops planning:

```
model: redwood-quant-70b
reserved_gpus: 12
autoscale:
  min_pool: 12
  max_pool: 24
  burst_credit_policy: allowed
  max_burst_gpus: 12
preheat:
  kv_warmup: true
  warmup_targets: top_5k_prompts
  warmup_window: 15m
```

ben_ops: This hedged approach keeps committed cost lower but gives headroom for spikes. Also recommend AZ spread 2-way to meet their multi-AZ ask.

carmen_sales: From pricing perspective, how does 12 reserved vs 16 reserved change unit economics? They asked for a monthly committed quote vs pay-as-you-go.

ben_ops: With our current pricing model, reserved commits reduce per-token bill by ~28–33% relative to on-demand (depends on length/mix). Burst (on-demand) is billed at on-demand rates + a small premium (we typically add ~10% on top of list). Quick example: if on-demand unit = $0.0008/token, reserved effective unit ~ $0.00055/token. These are illustrative — we'll run exact math in the quote once we have typical token mix.

anya_ml: Also factor in cost of preheat synthetic runs. Warmup traffic to fill KV cache consumes tokens and GPU time; budget 2–3% of daily token volume for warmup windows. But that saves a lot on tail latency and reduces burst GPU needs.

maria_legal: Security Qs: they require KMS for customer-managed keys, audit logs for inference requests (at least metadata), and SOC2-like retention on logs. For Private option we can offer VPC private control plane and HSM/KMS integration, but that'll be a separate contract and lead time for on-prem/VPC provisioning. Please confirm which scope they want in the questionnaire.

mike_sales: Good — I'll confirm with FinLedger they want KMS + audit metadata and multi-AZ. They're open to Private but want a pricing comparison.

ops_oncall: One ops note: ensure canary/circuit-breaker on autoscale — if burst uses spot capacity we need graceful fallback to a smaller model variant (e.g., 13B quant) if eviction happens. Recommend rollout policy:
- canary 5% traffic to new capacity for 10m
- fallback: model_variant_small if queueing > 200ms for >2m

deploy-bot: Reminder: Schedule a POC smoke test window (2h) with load generator. Use scenario: 600 qps peak for 10m, with 20% embeddings traffic and 80% chat. Preheat 30m before smoke.

mike_sales: Plan: I'll propose POC week next Tue-Wed. Action items: @ben_ops run a cost sketch for (12 reserved + burst to 24) vs (16 reserved + burst to 24) and include warmup token budget; @anya_ml sketch expected p95 reduction from KV warmup; @maria_legal draft short answers for the KMS/audit checklist we can paste into their questionnaire.

ben_ops: On it — will ping with numbers by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

anya_ml: I'll prepare a short summary (1-pager) on warmup + batching impact with expected p95 deltas.

maria_legal: I'll draft KMS/audit responses and include timeline for Private deployment (lead time ~6–8 weeks).

mike_sales: Awesome, thanks team. I'll keep FinLedger in the loop and schedule the smoke test once we have the cost sketch.
